window.description: Completion window for every row in the batch (`"15m"`, `"1h"`, or `"24h"`).

requests.description: One or more inference rows sharing the same `body.model`. Each `body` is normalized to chat-completions shape at create (Responses `input` → `messages`), validated, then enqueued. Invalid rows return HTTP 400 with `requests[i]` and optional `custom_id`.

results.description: Per-request outcomes when batch is completed or failed.

service_tier.description: Processing tier for the request. `"flex"` selects flex processing (beta) on flex-enabled accounts: discounted tokens in exchange for lower scheduling priority and best-effort completion — the request may queue significantly longer than default-tier requests, so raise your client timeout accordingly. A flex request that cannot complete in time fails with 408 (OpenAI SDKs retry it automatically). All other accepted values (`auto`, `default`, `scale`, `priority`) are served at the default tier. Responses echo the tier actually served in `service_tier`.

body.description: OpenAI-style request body. Must include `model`. Accepts chat completions shape (`messages`) or Responses shape (`input`); Responses fields are normalized to chat format at create, then validated before enqueue.

input.description: Input for the completion. Either a plain string (shorthand for a single user message) or an array of OpenAI Responses input items.

service_tier.description: Processing tier for the request. `"flex"` selects flex processing (beta) on flex-enabled accounts: discounted tokens in exchange for lower scheduling priority and best-effort completion — the request may queue significantly longer than default-tier requests, so raise your client timeout accordingly, or use `background: true` and poll. All other accepted values (`auto`, `default`, `scale`, `priority`) are served at the default tier. Responses echo the tier actually served in `service_tier`.
